More 500s follow, plus a 503 'reduce your request rate' (#199), and the AWS SDK exhausts its retry quota after 74 failed attempts in 60s (#185). This looks like an S3-side failure in us-east-1 rather than our code or config. template-svc's /render path only fails when it writes to S3. notification-svc then returns 'storage write failed' (#175, #201), and api-gateway surfaces 500s with 10-28s latency (#174, #182, #198). The failures are fast 500s, but the gateway latency suggests retries stacking up, so dependency_timeout is a plausible alternative.

The S3 errors may be amplified by the SDK retry storm (74 failed attempts in 60s, #185) and the 503 throttling (#199), with gateway latency of 10-28s pointing to retries stacking up in notification-svc and template-svc. If the S3 throttling is self-inflicted by this retry pattern, the root cause is cascading rather than an external outage.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check AWS S3 us-east-1 health status and request-id patterns. Mitigate by reducing template-svc S3 write concurrency and retry storms (the retry quota is already exhausted). Consider failing over to a fallback artifact store, or making template storage writes async/queued. Add a circuit breaker on the template-svc S3 path so notification-svc fails fast instead of holding gateway requests for 10-28s. Cap retries with jittered backoff.
